slides.title: Multi-Step Equations
slides.note: Post the learning target. Say one line and nothing else yet: “Today: multi-step equations with fractions and decimals.”

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Q4 is today's move in miniature: two-thirds of 9 is 6, so two-thirds of 9x is 6x. Say that in one sentence after the reveal — Example 2's Your Turn distributes a two-thirds. Two minutes silent, then reveal, no discussion.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Reveal. Ask for the band each question came from only if time allows.

slides.title: Vocabulary
slides.sub: The new words, before they are used.
slides.note: Two words for today's numbers. A common denominator is the number that clears every fraction at once — 6 for halves and thirds, 15 for thirds and fifths. A rational coefficient is just a fraction or a decimal in front of the variable; the moves of the last three days do not change.

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
The order of the last three days, said once as a list: distribute; collect like terms on each side; move the x-terms to one side and the constants to the other; divide; check. Here the left is 6x − 12 + 5 = 6x − 7 and the right is 2x + 12 + 1 = 2x + 13. Take 2x from both sides and add 7: 4x = 20, so x = 5. Check in both sides of the first equation: 3(6) + 5 = 23 and 2(11) + 1 = 23.
OFF: 'Distribute, collect, move, divide, check. Every equation, every time.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
Two ways with a fraction. First: distribute it — one-third of 6x is 2x and one-third of 9 is 3, every term inside, just as a whole number would. Then 2x + 3 = x + 7 and x = 4. Second: multiply BOTH sides by a common denominator. Halves and thirds clear with 6, and the 6 multiplies EVERY term — the 3 and the 5 as well as the fractions: 3x + 18 = 2x + 30, so x = 12. Check: 6 + 3 = 9 and 4 + 5 = 9. A board that writes 3x + 3 = 2x + 5 multiplied only the fractions.
OFF: 'A fraction outside the parentheses multiplies every term inside. A common denominator multiplies every term on both sides.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
The 0.5 multiplies the 8x AND the −6: 4x − 3. Then the x-terms: take 1.5x from both sides, 2.5x on the left; add 3: 2.5x = 5, so x = 2. Check: 0.5(16 − 6) = 5 and 1.5(2) + 2 = 5. This is the skill the state scored lowest on its released Grade 8 test — almost four in five students missed it — and the miss is nearly always 4x − 6: the decimal never reached the second term.
OFF: 'The decimal is a number like any other. It multiplies every term inside.'

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Ask what each side is once it is distributed and collected, before anyone moves a term.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Each side first: the left is 6x + 2 − 4x = 2x + 2, the right 3x − 6 + 1 = 3x − 5. Take 2x (the smaller) from both sides: 2 = x − 5, so x = 7. Check in both sides of the first equation: 2(22) − 28 = 16 and 3(5) + 1 = 16. A board with x = 3 wrote 3x − 2 on the right (the 3 to one term only); one with x = −5 wrote 3x + 6 (the sign).

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: The left is 4x + 8 − x = 3x + 8, the right 2x − 6 + 20 = 2x + 14. Take 2x: x + 8 = 14, so x = 6. Check: 4(8) − 6 = 26 and 2(3) + 20 = 26. This catches a student who collects across the equals sign, and the one-term distribution: 4x + 2 − x on the left gives x = 12.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Example 2
slides.sub: A fraction in front of the parentheses.
slides.note: Ask what three-fourths of 8x is, and what three-fourths of −4 is, before anyone writes.

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: Three-fourths of 8x is 6x; three-fourths of −4 is −3 — every term inside, as with a whole number. Then take 2x from both sides: 4x − 3 = 9, so 4x = 12 and x = 3. Check: three-fourths of 20 is 15, and 2(3) + 9 = 15. A board with x = 3.25 wrote 6x − 4 (the fraction to one term only); one with x = 1.5 wrote 6x + 3 (the sign).

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: Two-thirds of 9x is 6x and two-thirds of −6 is −4: 6x − 4 = 2x + 12. Take 2x: 4x − 4 = 12, so 4x = 16 and x = 4. Check: two-thirds of 30 is 20, and 2(4) + 12 = 20. A board with x = 4.5 wrote 6x − 6 (the two-thirds never reached the 6).

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Notes I's order with whole numbers. A board with x = 10/3 wrote 5x − 2 (the 5 to one term only); one with x = −2/3 wrote 5x + 10 (the sign). Check: 5(4) + 3 = 23 and 2(6) + 11 = 23.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: Notes II's first way: half of 10x is 5x and half of 8 is 4. A board with x = 3 wrote 5x + 8 (the half to one term only); one with x = 9 took the 4 the wrong way (2x = 18). Check: half of 58 is 29, and 3(5) + 14 = 29.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: Notes III with new numbers — the 21% skill. 0.4 of 5x is 2x and 0.4 of −10 is −4. A board with x = 13 wrote 2x − 10 (the decimal to one term only — the state's most common miss); one with x = −1 wrote 2x + 4 (the sign). Check: 0.4(25) = 10 and 7 + 3 = 10.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic. Option D is the sign, option C the one-term distribution, option B a term carried across the equals sign without its sign changing. On a split: sixty seconds to think again, re-vote — then check 4 in both sides: −2(12 − 5) = −14 and 16 − 30 = −14.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: Notes II's second way: thirds and fifths clear with 15, and the 15 multiplies every term — the 1s as well. A board with x = 1 multiplied only the fractions (5x − 1 = 3x + 1); one stuck at 2x = 30 wrote the answer before dividing. Check: 15/3 − 1 = 4 and 15/5 + 1 = 4.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic, and 11.03's endings with a fraction. Both sides are 3x − 2, so every number works. Option A distributed the 3 to one term and found 'no solution' — ask what 3 times −1 is. Options D and B read the true ending as an x. On a split: sixty seconds to think again, re-vote.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: The extra-number board (ruling 22): Shop B's 3 blocks are not needed. Each shop's cost is an expression in h; they cost the same when the expressions are equal, 12 + 4.5h = 7.5h. Take 4.5h (the smaller) from both sides. Check: both cost \$30 for 4 hours.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: Backwards: the solution is given and a number in the equation is missing. Put 2 in for x on BOTH sides — the right is 24, so 2 + □ must be 8. Check: 3(2 + 6) = 24 and 2(2) + 20 = 24.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.sub: Take your time. Boards up when you have written it.
slides.note: Written, and the exit evidence. Read two aloud: one that distributes the 1.5 to both terms and checks in the first equation, and one whose check caught its own slip. The decimal is the 21% skill; the check is what proves the answer.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Independent Set
slides.sub: Six questions. On your own, in writing.
slides.note: Hand out the Independent Set; the same six questions are on the board. Silent work. Circulate and mark what you see; do not teach. Whatever is not finished goes home.

slides.title: IXL
slides.note: IXL: every listed skill is required, SmartScore 67. Due by the Unit 11 test.
